The most likely corrupted element is **M2**, with its gate on the R2/Q3 node (`e3`). Its drain is at `g`, so the gate-to-drain path forms a loop back to `vref` through R2. Raising `vref` raises `e3`, which turns M2 on harder, which pulls `g` down and pushes `vref` higher. That is positive feedback, which fits both the line-regulation failure and the failed start-up. I haven't simulated this, so the ranking is a reasoned guess from the netlist.

R2 and Mst3 are the next candidates if the gate wiring is correct."}
